builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SWAP-INR: Implicit Neural Representation with Switchable Attention Paths for Time-varying Multivariate Scientific Data Compression
summary: This method replaces traditional lossy compressors and standard implicit neural representations (INRs) for time-varying multivariate scientific simulation data. It costs the engineering effort of training a specialized architecture and requires post-training 16-bit quantization to maintain a constrained memory footprint. It can fail when applied to data lacking the specific cross-variable interactions of physics simulations, or when deployment targets lack support for the custom attention-based decoding process.
rationale: This technique is designed for scientific simulation data compression in HPC environments, which falls outside the scope of standard AI/ML production workloads involving model inference, training, or data processing.
technique: SWAP-INR: Neural Compression for Scientific Data

claims.statement: This method replaces traditional lossy compressors and standard implicit neural representations (INRs) for time-varying multivariate scientific simulation data. It costs the engineering effort of training a specialized architecture and requires post-training 16-bit quantization to maintain a constrained memory footprint. It can fail when applied to data lacking the specific cross-variable interactions of physics simulations, or when deployment targets lack support for the custom attention-based decoding process.
Achieves state-of-the-art compression performance on small modular reactor (SMR) datasets and competitive results on public physics simulation datasets.
